words-large.purpose: What is being said now, under 70 characters, and the empty-state invitation.

words-medium.purpose: Lines of 70 to 149 characters, and every system or error message.

words-small.purpose: Lines of 150 characters or more, capped at 190pt tall.

status-stamp.purpose: The one word naming the phase.

type-field.purpose: The typed draft on the stage.

transcript.purpose: Lines in the conversation, 2pt extra leading for yours and 4pt for replies.

error-line.purpose: Transcript errors, with a warning symbol.

action.purpose: Words in wisps, and mic notices.

small-print.purpose: The hint line, tool notes, the cut-in note and the model menu.

puck-snippet.purpose: The words in flight under the floating face.

motion.name: phase-wave
motion.purpose: The dark wave a phase change sends from the mouth. Strength 1 for a new ground, 0.6 entering hearing or speaking, 2.4 on cut-in.

motion.name: lurch
motion.purpose: The head throwing itself forward when you cut in.

motion.name: blink
motion.purpose: Blinks, and a blink on a change of phase.

motion.name: fog-drift
motion.purpose: The planes of fog, each at its own speed.

motion.name: wisp-firm
motion.purpose: A wisp condensing under the pointer.

motion.name: doze
motion.purpose: Left alone, it dozes off and drawing stops.

components.name: Wisp Action
components.description: The standard stage control: a word in a thin wisp of mist that thickens under the pointer.
components.css: .ds-wisp { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; height: 26px; padding: 0 6px; background: none; border: 0; color: #E9ECF1; font: 500 13px 'Avenir Next', -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; isolation: isolate; } .ds-wisp::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -6px -14px; z-index: -1; background: radial-gradient(ellipse closest-side, #A9B2C2 35%, transparent); filter: blur(5px); opacity: 0.17; transition: opacity 0.22s ease-out, transform 0.22s ease-out; } .ds-wisp:hover::before, .ds-wisp:focus-visible::before { opacity: 0.3; transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-wisp:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-wisp:disabled { opacity: 0.55; }

components.name: Top Bar Icon
components.description: A bare symbol in the top bar that gains a firm puff of mist on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-top-icon" aria-label="New conversation"><svg width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M4 20h4L19 9l-4-4L4 16z"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-top-icon { position: relative; width: 28px; height: 24px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: none; border: 0; color: #E9ECF1; cursor: pointer; isolation: isolate; } .ds-top-icon::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -4px -3px; z-index: -1; background: radial-gradient(ellipse closest-side, #A9B2C2 40%, transparent); filter: blur(3px); opacity: 0; transition: opacity 0.18s ease-out; } .ds-top-icon:hover::before, .ds-top-icon:focus-visible::before { opacity: 0.3; } .ds-top-icon:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-top-icon:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

components.name: Type Field
components.description: The typed draft in Didot on a firm puff of mist, replacing the action row.
components.css: .ds-type { position: relative; padding: 8px 10px; width: 320px; isolation: isolate; } .ds-type::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -6px; z-index: -1; background: radial-gradient(ellipse closest-side, #A9B2C2 60%, transparent); filter: blur(5px); opacity: 0.3; } .ds-type-input { width: 100%; background: none; border: 0; outline: none; color: #E9ECF1; font: 400 22px Didot, ui-serif, serif; } .ds-type-input::placeholder { color: rgba(233, 236, 241, 0.7); } .ds-type-input:focus-visible { caret-color: #E9ECF1; }

components.name: Status Stamp
components.description: The one word naming the phase, in Didot italic in the free dark at top left.
components.css: .ds-stamp { color: #E9ECF1; font: italic 400 24px Didot, ui-serif, serif; }

components.name: Words in the Dark
components.description: What is being said now, set straight on the dark in the speaker's ink.
components.html: It's about minus eight at the summit, with strong winds and clear skies.
components.css: .ds-words { max-width: 460px; margin: 0; padding: 18px 22px; background: #07080C; color: #D8CFA8; font: 400 34px/1.18 Didot, ui-serif, serif; }

components.name: Fog Bank Transcript
components.description: The conversation with no bubbles: yours right in cold white, replies left in long bone.
components.html:
Have people skied down it?

Yes, plenty. There's a ski resort on its southern slopes.
components.css: .ds-bank { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 18px; width: 460px; padding: 14px 22px 16px; background: linear-gradient(transparent, #07080C 3%); font: 500 16px 'Avenir Next', -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-bank p { margin: 0; } .ds-you { align-self: flex-end; max-width: 400px; text-align: right; color: #E9ECF1; } .ds-reply { max-width: 480px; color: #D8D2BC; line-height: 1.5; }

components.name: Floating Face Caption
components.description: The floating face's status on firm mist backed by a darkened layer, readable over any desktop.
components.css: .ds-puck { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 0 8px; color: #E9ECF1; font: italic 400 13px Didot, ui-serif, serif; isolation: isolate; } .ds-puck::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -8px -14px; z-index: -1; background: radial-gradient(ellipse closest-side, rgba(7, 8, 12, 0.9) 55%, transparent), radial-gradient(ellipse closest-side, rgba(169, 178, 194, 0.3) 55%, transparent); filter: blur(3px); }

components.name: Personality Chip
components.description: A Settings chip, the one place a pill is allowed, filled cherry when selected.
components.css: .ds-chip { height: 26px; padding: 0 10px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: rgba(127, 127, 127, 0.14); color: inherit; font: 500 12px -apple-system, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { background: rgba(127, 127, 127, 0.22); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #B5122A; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chip-on, .ds-chip-on:hover { background: #B5122A; color: #FFFFFF; }

narrative.overview:
The window is a cold black room with something in it. A wasted, real-looking head hangs in fog, lit from one side so that half of it is lost, dissolving at its edges and slightly askew. Its eyes find your pointer and follow it slowly. When it speaks, its lips move with the voice you are actually hearing, and the mouth opens further than a jaw should on crooked, stained, partly missing teeth.

Density is low. There is one status word in Didot italic, the words being said in Didot, and a few controls that are only thin wisps of mist with a word in them. Colour barely exists: near-black ground, grey fog, bone relief, and blood only in the flesh and in the red dark of Thinking. The register is serious, mysterious and creepy, and the owner has rejected a cute version as childish.

The stage is almost still, then rarely violent. Everything drifts slowly, one dark wave leaves the mouth when the phase changes, and the head only moves fast in the lurch when you cut in. All of it is one Metal fragment shader reading one noise texture, so a long conversation costs the GPU the same as a short one, and drawing stops when the window is hidden or the face has dozed off. Settings is deliberately outside this world: native macOS forms with a cherry tint.
keyCharacteristics: A near-black ground that changes whole, turning oxblood while it thinks
A head of bone-grey relief, lit from one side, dissolving into fog at its edges
Lips and ripples driven only by live audio
Wet, bloodshot, milky eyes that look through the fog and follow the pointer anywhere on screen
Didot for large words, Avenir Next medium for small ones, cold white for you and bone for the reply
Controls as thin wisps of mist, with no pills, glass or hard edges, and the whole window as the talk control

rules.name: The Whole Dark Rule
rules.body: A phase colour changes the entire ground, never a badge, dot or patch on it. The conversation's fog bank stays Void, so with it open only the band above the bank changes and the status word carries the phase.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Cold white is you and bone is the reply, in words and ripples alike. System messages on the stage are cold white. Bone's only other uses are transcript errors and the copied checkmark.

rules.name: The Cherry Stays Out Rule
rules.body: Cherry belongs to Settings. The stage's reds are flesh and the oxblood dark, and interface elements on the stage never use them.

rules.name: The Inscription Rule
rules.body: Set by size: 21pt and up is Didot, below that is Avenir Next medium. The italic stamp is the one exception, and it stays in its two places, at 24pt on the stage and 13pt on the puck's backed mist.

rules.name: The Whole String Rule
rules.body: Didot and Avenir Next are Latin only, so any string containing an alphabetic character at or above U+0250 falls back whole to the system face at the same size, serif at 21pt and up. Never let their punctuation mix into another script, and pass the string to the font choice wherever the text is user or model content.

rules.name: The Size by Length Rule
rules.body: On the stage, text size follows length (34, 26, then 21pt) rather than role, so a short answer is an inscription and a long one still fits.

rules.name: The One Side Rule
rules.body: The key light comes from the upper left and leaves the far half of the face in shadow. The only other light is a faint cold fill from below, so the shadows never go quite flat. Never add a second key or a rim.

rules.name: The Eyes Look Through Rule
rules.body: The eyes are drawn in front of the fog and the ripples. Whatever else the fog hides, it never covers the gaze.

rules.name: The Dissolving Edge Rule
rules.body: The head has no outline. It ends where its height falls into the noise, and while thinking or dozing it sinks back, to a little over half its opacity at the most.

rules.name: The Real Voice Rule
rules.body: Lips and ripples come from the sound actually happening, never from a canned loop or the text. With no audio, the mouth rests and the fog stays quiet.

rules.name: The One Wave Rule
rules.body: A phase change sends one dark wave from the mouth at 1400pt a second, with the new dark inside and the old outside and a soft 52pt edge. A change of ground strikes at full strength, entering hearing or speaking at 0.6, and cutting in at 2.4 with no change of colour. A new wave replaces the last.

rules.name: The Mist Control Rule
rules.body: Stage controls are words in mist, with no fill, border or edge you could trace. Hovering makes the mist thicken, and nothing else about the word changes.

rules.name: The No Mic Button Rule
rules.body: Talking starts from a click on the window or floating face, Space, the global shortcut or the menu bar item, never from a dedicated button in the window. Mute mic is a word, and it appears only once the mic is on.

rules.name: The Native Settings Rule
rules.body: Settings is where the app stops performing. Add the cherry tint and the Didot header, and leave the rest to the system. The past-conversations popover and the menus stay native too.

dos: Do drive lips and ripples from the sound actually happening, in the owner's ink.
Do change state by changing the whole dark or the face, and pair it with its status word.
Do keep the head real, askew and lit from one side, dissolving at its edges.
Do set stage text straight on the dark, with the fog calmed behind it.
Do make a new stage control a word in a wisp of mist.
Do use the system face for the whole string when text contains any non-Latin script.
Do keep Settings native, adding only the cherry tint and the Didot pane header.
Do respect Reduce Motion and stop drawing when idle or hidden: the language model needs the GPU.
donts: Don't add a glowing orb or blob, a friendly avatar, or a round mic button.
Don't make it cute or cartoonish: the owner rejected the cloud as childish.
Don't put cards, pills, glass or hard-edged containers on the stage.
Don't add shadows to text or controls.
Don't use cherry on the stage, or set interface elements in the flesh reds.
Don't add a second key light, or a second concurrent wave.
Don't make the head or the fog move fast: besides the voice-driven lips and blinks, only the lurch and the wave are quick.
Don't add a button to start talking.
